claims.claim: An explicit trusted decision returned by resolveProjectTrust is honored after bootstrap: both true and false decisions are transferred to the settings manager instead of being overwritten by a hardcoded value.
claims.verification: .prale-eval/regression.mjs checks 'explicit trusted decision is honored after bootstrap' and 'explicit untrusted decision keeps project extensions excluded'

claims.claim: Settings are reloaded for the decided trust state before the final resource resolution, so package resolution and the final extension set observe the decision.
claims.verification: .prale-eval/regression.mjs check 'settings reload for the decided trust state precedes the final resolution'

claims.claim: Project extensions stay excluded during the bootstrap pass that feeds resolveProjectTrust, and the preloaded user/CLI extensions are reused by the final pass instead of being reloaded.
claims.verification: .prale-eval/regression.mjs check 'bootstrap pass excludes project extensions while loading user and CLI ones'

deliverables.change: One-line repair in DefaultResourceLoader.reload(): after `const projectTrusted = await options.resolveProjectTrust(...)`, call `this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted)` instead of the hardcoded `this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false)`. The existing settings reload and final resource resolution that follow now run for the decided trust state; the bootstrap pass still forces untrusted settings and reuses its preloaded extensions.

Standalone Node assertion script (node:assert/strict, no dependencies) that drives the real DefaultResourceLoader.reload() through the .prale-eval/subject.mjs boundary fakes and asserts bootstrap exclusion, honored true and false decisions, settings reload ordering before final resolution, and no-trust-prompt behavior.

validation.notes: Run from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0; exit code 0 with all 5 assertions groups passing (`ok - ...` for each, then `all 5 trust-transfer checks passed`). The script loads the real packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts via the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs helper (Node 24 stripTypeScriptTypes + vm SourceTextModule with explicit boundary fakes for settings/package/extension loading), so it exercises production code rather than a reimplementation. Fault discrimination was verified by temporarily reverting the target line to `setProjectTrusted(false)`: the script then failed with AssertionError 'resolveProjectTrust(true) must leave the project trusted' (false !== true) and exit code 1; re-applying the repair restored a clean pass. The assertions compare rebuilt local arrays because extension lists cross the VM realm. Limitations: the repository's vitest suites (e.g. packages/coding-agent/test/resource-loader.test.ts) were not executed because workspace dependencies are not installed and installing them is out of scope for this task, and tsc type checking was likewise skipped; the regression script itself needs no dependencies or network.
